caption: LUM-1274 — `/scoped-models` ("Model Configuration") on the Rust port: the panel that consumes the last six silent `app.*` chords. Real binary + real PTY + pyte VT emulator, same harness / parser / binary as LUM-1286/1293/1294/1298/1308. Scene 1 is the shipped startup header; scene 2 hides it (Alt+H) and opens the panel, because the selector overlay is clipped to the transcript viewport and the 21-row startup header would cut the footer off (the filed P0 LUM-1262); scenes 3-9 walk the chord families.
notes: The child's HOME is a fresh temp dir (the harness default), so Ctrl+S writes a throwaway settings.json and the developer's real config is untouched.
A footer count (`0/192 enabled`, `all enabled`, `(unsaved)`) can only be printed after the panel state actually changed, so those assertions are the chord's proof, not the frame's.
Scenes 7-8 are the reorder pair: the same filtered window before and after Alt+Down, with the two enabled rows swapping places.

panels.label: 1. shipped startup header on the post-LUM-1308 binary (unchanged by this round)
2. Alt+H hides the header, /scoped-models opens the panel: title, checked rows with provider column, key legend footer
expect: Enter toggle · Ctrl+A enable all · Ctrl+X clear all
Ctrl+P toggle provider · Alt+Up / Alt+Down reorder · Ctrl+S save
Session-only. Ctrl+S to save to settings.

panels.label: 3. Enter (tui.select.confirm) toggles the highlighted model off — panel stays open, footer flips to (unsaved)
6. Ctrl+P (app.models.toggleProvider) on the highlighted ant-ling row disables that whole provider
7. Ctrl+X then Enter on row 0 and row 1: the scope is exactly the two ant-ling Ling models, in catalog order
8. Alt+Down (app.models.reorderDown) moves the highlighted model below its neighbour — the two rows swap, the (N/192) scroll counter moves with them
9. Ctrl+S (app.models.save) persists the scope to settings.json — the footer says so and drops (unsaved)
